choices: If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well
If he sees me, he will send me away
If I ask, the crowd will stop me
If I wait, he will come to my house
quiz.explain: Mark 5:28. She reached out in faith.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus tell Jairus when news came that his daughter had died?
choices: Go home and mourn with your family
quiz.explain: Mark 5:36: "Don’t be afraid, only believe."

quiz.prompt: What does "Talitha cumi" mean?
choices: Girl, I tell you, get up!
quiz.explain: Mark 5:41. Mark keeps Jesus' own words in Aramaic, the language he spoke, and translates them.

lessons.title: Sheep without a shepherd
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
The disciples come back from their first mission tired, with no time even to eat. Jesus says, "Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile." But the crowds get there first (Mark 6:33). Instead of being annoyed, Jesus "had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd."

He teaches them, and as evening comes, he feeds them. Five loaves and two fish are blessed, broken and handed out, and "They all ate and were filled." Jesus cares about both: his tired friends who need rest, and a hungry crowd. And he feeds the crowd through his disciples' hands, with what they already had.

**Reflection:** What small thing do you have, like five loaves and two fish, that you could offer to God today?

*Study aid: apart from the resurrection itself, the feeding of the five thousand is the only miracle told in all four Gospels (compare John 6:9).*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you care when I am tired and when I am hungry. Take the little I have and use it.

quiz.prompt: Why did Jesus have compassion on the crowd?
choices: they were like sheep without a shepherd
they had come from far away
quiz.explain: Mark 6:34. Jesus saw people with no one to guide them.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus first invite his tired disciples to do?
quiz.explain: Mark 6:31: "Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile."

quiz.prompt: "They all ate and were ___."
quiz.explain: Mark 6:42. Everyone had enough.

lessons.title: It is I
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
After feeding the crowd, Jesus sends the disciples across the lake and goes up a mountain to pray (Mark 6:46). In the night he sees them "distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them," and comes to them, walking on the sea.

They think he is a ghost and cry out. His answer is immediate: "Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid." He gets into the boat, and the wind stops. Mark adds an honest detail: they still had not understood about the loaves (Mark 6:52). The disciples are slow learners, which may be a comfort to the rest of us.

**Reflection:** Where are you straining at the oars right now? What would it mean to hear Jesus say, "Don’t be afraid"?

*Study aid: the "fourth watch of the night" (Mark 6:48) was the last part of the night, roughly from three to six in the morning.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, come to me where I am straining. Let me hear you say: it is I, don't be afraid.

quiz.prompt: Why were the disciples struggling as they rowed?
choices: the wind was contrary to them
quiz.explain: Mark 6:48: "Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them."

quiz.prompt: What did the disciples think when they saw Jesus walking on the sea?
quiz.explain: Mark 6:49: they "supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out."

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus say to them?
choices: Wait for me on the shore
Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid
Why did you leave without me?
quiz.explain: Mark 6:50: "Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid."

lessons.title: Be opened
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
People bring Jesus a man who is deaf and can hardly speak. Jesus takes him away from the crowd, privately. Then he does something very physical and personal: he puts his fingers in the man's ears, touches his tongue, looks up to heaven and sighs.

"Ephphatha!" he says, which means, "Be opened!" The man hears and speaks clearly. Many readers notice how Jesus heals him away from the crowd, in a way that respects him. The people's verdict could stand over everything Mark has told so far: "He has done all things well."

**Reflection:** Jesus gives this man his full, personal attention, away from the crowd. Where would you most like that kind of attention from him today?

*Study aid: the crowd's words, "He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!" echo a promise in Isaiah 35:5-6 about what God would one day do.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, thank you for your personal care. Meet me today in the place where I need you most.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus do first with the man who was deaf?
choices: told him to wash his ears
took him aside from the multitude privately
asked the crowd to pray for him
quiz.explain: Mark 7:33. Jesus meets him away from the crowd.

quiz.prompt: What does "Ephphatha" mean?
quiz.explain: Mark 7:34: “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”

quiz.prompt: What did the astonished people say in verse 37?
choices: He has done all things well
quiz.explain: Mark 7:37: "He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!"

lessons.title: Who do you say I am?
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Ever since the storm on the lake, the disciples' question has hung over the story: who is this (Mark 4:41)? Now Jesus asks it himself. First he asks what people are saying. The answers are respectful: John the Baptizer, Elijah, one of the prophets.

Then he makes it personal: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answers, "You are the Christ." Many readers see this as the turning point of Mark. From here Jesus begins to tell his disciples plainly that he will suffer, die and rise again (Mark 8:31), and the road turns toward Jerusalem.

**Reflection:** Other people's opinions about Jesus are easy to repeat. If he asked you today, "But who do you say that I am?", how would you answer in your own words?

*Study aid: "Christ" comes from a Greek word meaning anointed one, the same meaning as the Hebrew word Messiah. Many Jews of the time hoped for an anointed king from David's family.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, I want to know you for myself, not only what others say. Show me who you are.

quiz.prompt: According to the disciples, who did some people say Jesus was?
quiz.explain: Mark 8:28: "John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others, one of the prophets."

quiz.prompt: Peter answered, "You are the ___."
quiz.explain: Mark 8:29: Peter answered, "You are the Christ."

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus ask his disciples in Mark 8:29?
choices: But who do you say that I am?
quiz.explain: Mark 8:29. Jesus moves from what others say to what his friends believe.

lessons.title: Take up your cross
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Right after Peter calls him the Christ, Jesus explains what kind of Christ he will be: one who "must suffer many things," be killed, "and after three days rise again." Peter is horrified and tries to correct him (Mark 8:32).

Then Jesus tells the crowd what following him means: "let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me." In his day, a person carrying a cross was walking to execution. It is not a call to go looking for pain, or to stay where you are being harmed, but to put Jesus ahead of our own comfort and plans. And there is a paradox: "whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it."

**Reflection:** What is one way you could set aside your own way today, for Jesus' sake or for someone else's?

*Study aid: on the road to Jerusalem Jesus foretells his death and resurrection three times (Mark 8:31, Mark 9:31 and Mark 10:33-34). Each time, the disciples struggle to understand.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, teach me to follow you even when it costs me something. Help me trust that life is found in you.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus say the Son of Man must do?
quiz.explain: Mark 8:31: "the Son of Man must suffer many things."

quiz.prompt: "let him deny himself, and take up his ___, and follow me."
quiz.explain: Mark 8:34. Following Jesus means taking up the cross.

quiz.prompt: According to Mark 8:35, who will save his life?
choices: whoever will lose his life for my sake
quiz.explain: Mark 8:35. Life is found by losing it for Jesus and the Good News.

lessons.title: Listen to him
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Six days later, Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and they see him "changed into another form." Moses and Elijah appear and talk with him. Peter, frightened and not knowing what to say, suggests making three tents (Mark 9:5).

Then a cloud covers them, and a voice speaks: "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him." When it is over, "they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only." After the glory, they are left with Jesus and with one instruction: listen. They will need it, because the road ahead goes down the mountain and toward the cross.

**Reflection:** Where do you need to listen to Jesus today, rather than talk, plan or fix things?

*Study aid: this scene is often called the Transfiguration. Many readers see Moses and Elijah as standing for the Law and the Prophets, the Hebrew Scriptures.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, quiet me enough to listen to you today.

quiz.prompt: Who appeared and talked with Jesus on the mountain?
quiz.explain: Mark 9:4: "Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus."

quiz.prompt: "This is my beloved Son. ___ to him."
quiz.explain: Mark 9:7: "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him."

quiz.prompt: Whom did the disciples see when they looked around afterward?
quiz.explain: Mark 9:8: "they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only."

lessons.title: Help my unbelief
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Down from the mountain, a desperate father is waiting. His son has suffered since childhood, and the disciples could not help. He says to Jesus, "if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."

Jesus picks up his words: "If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes." The father's reply is a prayer many people have made their own: "I believe. Help my unbelief!" He doesn't pretend to have perfect faith. He brings the faith he has, mixed with doubt, and asks for help with both. And Jesus helps him.

**Reflection:** Is there an area where your faith and your doubt live side by side? You can pray this father's prayer, just as it is.

*Study aid: afterwards the disciples ask privately why they could not help the boy, and Jesus speaks to them about prayer (Mark 9:28-29).*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Lord, I believe. Help my unbelief.

quiz.prompt: How long had the boy been suffering?
quiz.explain: Mark 9:21: He said, "From childhood."

quiz.prompt: "I believe. Help my ___!"
quiz.explain: Mark 9:24. The father brings both his faith and his doubt.

quiz.prompt: What did the father ask Jesus to do?
choices: take my son to the priest
pray for us at the temple
have compassion on us and help us
quiz.explain: Mark 9:22: "But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."

lessons.title: Let the children come
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
People bring little children for Jesus to bless, and the disciples try to stop them. In that culture children had little standing, and perhaps the disciples thought Jesus had more important work to do.

Jesus is "moved with indignation." "Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these." Then he takes them in his arms and blesses them. God's Kingdom, he says, is received "like a little child": not earned by status, but received with open hands.

**Reflection:** What would it mean for you to receive from God like a child, without first trying to prove you deserve it?

*Study aid: Christians have drawn different practical conclusions from this passage, for example about children in worship. All agree that Jesus welcomed them.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, teach me to come to you like a child, with open hands.

quiz.prompt: What did the disciples do when people brought children to Jesus?
choices: rebuked those who were bringing them
lined them up to meet him
quiz.explain: Mark 10:13. The disciples tried to keep the children away.

quiz.prompt: How did Jesus feel when he saw it?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:14: "when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation."

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus do with the children?
choices: took them in his arms and blessed them
sent them home to their parents
quiz.explain: Mark 10:16: "He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them."

lessons.title: One thing you lack
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
A man runs up and kneels before Jesus with a big question: "what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?" He says he has kept the commandments since his youth (Mark 10:20). Then Mark adds a detail that is easy to miss: "Jesus looking at him loved him."

Out of that love comes a hard word: "One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor." The man goes away sad, "for he was one who had great possessions." The disciples are astonished and ask who can be saved at all (Mark 10:26). Jesus answers, "With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God."

**Reflection:** Is there anything you hold so tightly that it would be hard to follow Jesus without it?

*Study aid: Jesus does not give this exact instruction to everyone in the Gospels. Christians have long discussed how it applies today; many see in it a warning about trusting in riches (Mark 10:24).*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you look at me with love. Loosen my grip on whatever keeps me from following you.

quiz.prompt: What does Mark say Jesus did as he looked at the man?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:21: "Jesus looking at him loved him."

quiz.prompt: Why did the man go away sorrowful?
choices: his family would not let him
he was one who had great possessions
quiz.explain: Mark 10:22: "he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions."

quiz.prompt: How did Jesus answer the astonished disciples in verse 27?
choices: Only those who keep every law
Only those who give everything away
With men it is impossible, but not with God
quiz.explain: Mark 10:27: "for all things are possible with God."

lessons.title: Not to be served
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
James and John have just asked for the best seats in Jesus' glory, and the other ten are angry with them (Mark 10:37 and Mark 10:41). Jesus calls them all together and sets two kinds of greatness side by side.

Rulers of the nations "lord it over" people. "But it shall not be so among you." Among Jesus' followers the great one is the servant, and the first is the one who serves everyone. Then he points to himself: "For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many." Many readers see this verse as a key to the whole of Mark.

**Reflection:** Where could you serve someone today without being asked and without being noticed?

*Study aid: a ransom was a price paid to set a captive free. Christians have understood how Jesus' death is a ransom in a number of ways; Mark gives the picture without a full explanation.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you came to serve. Make me willing to serve too, especially where no one will notice.

quiz.prompt: "For the Son of Man also came not to be ___ but to serve"
quiz.explain: Mark 10:45. Jesus describes his own life as service.

quiz.prompt: In Mark 10:43, whoever wants to become great among you shall be…
quiz.explain: Mark 10:43: "whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant."

quiz.prompt: What does Jesus say he came to give, in verse 45?
choices: his life as a ransom for many
quiz.explain: Mark 10:45: "and to give his life as a ransom for many."

lessons.title: What do you want?
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Bartimaeus is blind and begging by the road out of Jericho (Mark 10:46). When he hears that Jesus is passing, he shouts, "Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!" People tell him to be quiet. He shouts louder.

Jesus stops and calls him. Then he asks a question with an obvious answer: "What do you want me to do for you?" He lets Bartimaeus say it in his own words: "that I may see again." He receives his sight, and Mark ends with a quiet detail: he "followed Jesus on the way." The road leads to Jerusalem, and Bartimaeus is now walking it.

**Reflection:** If Jesus asked you today, "What do you want me to do for you?", what would you say?

*Study aid: "son of David" was a title for the promised king from David's family. Bartimaeus is the first person in Mark to call Jesus by it.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me. Help me to see, and to follow you on the way.

quiz.prompt: What did Bartimaeus do when the crowd told him to be quiet?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:48: "he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”"

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus ask Bartimaeus?
choices: What do you want me to do for you?
Who told you I was here?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:51. Jesus invites him to say what he needs.

quiz.prompt: What did Bartimaeus do after he received his sight?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:52: "Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus on the way."

lessons.title: Hosanna
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Jesus enters Jerusalem riding a young donkey. People spread their garments and branches on the road, the way a king might be welcomed, and the crowd shouts, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!"

It is a joyful scene, and an unusual one. A king arriving on a borrowed donkey (Mark 11:3) is not what most people pictured. Many readers hear an echo of Zechariah 9:9, where Israel's king comes "lowly, and riding on a donkey." Within a week, the city that welcomed him will see him crucified. Christians see both truths in this scene: Jesus is the king, and his way to the throne goes through the cross.

**Reflection:** What kind of king do you want Jesus to be? What kind of king does he show himself to be here?

*Study aid: "Hosanna" comes from a Hebrew phrase meaning save us. By Jesus' time it may also have become a shout of praise. The crowd's words echo Psalm 118:25-26.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you come humbly. I welcome you as my king, on your terms and not mine.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus ride into Jerusalem?
quiz.explain: Mark 11:7: "They brought the young donkey to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it."

quiz.prompt: What did many people spread on the road?
quiz.explain: Mark 11:8: "Many spread their garments on the way."

quiz.prompt: "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the ___!"
quiz.explain: Mark 11:9. The crowd welcomes Jesus with words from Psalm 118.

lessons.title: All she had
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Jesus sits opposite the temple treasury and watches people give. Rich people put in large amounts. Then a poor widow drops in two tiny coins.

Jesus calls his disciples over, as if to make sure they don't miss it: "this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury." The others gave "out of their abundance"; she gave "all that she had to live on." Jesus measures a gift differently. What he notices is not its size but what it cost her. Many readers also see trust in it.

**Reflection:** What would it look like to give God something that really matters to you, whether time, attention or money, as an act of trust?

*Study aid: just before this, Jesus warns about scribes who "devour widows’ houses" (Mark 12:40). Some readers also hear in this scene a lament over a system that left her so poor.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: God, everything I have comes from you. Teach me to see giving the way Jesus sees it.

quiz.prompt: What did the poor widow put into the treasury?
quiz.explain: Mark 12:42: "she cast in two small brass coins."

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus say the poor widow did?
choices: gave only so that she would be seen
gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury
gave less than anyone else that day
gave more than the law required of her
quiz.explain: Mark 12:43: "this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury."

quiz.prompt: According to verse 44, how did the widow give?
quiz.explain: Mark 12:44: "she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on."

lessons.title: What she could
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Jesus has just warned his disciples about hard days ahead and told them to stay alert, since "of that day or that hour no one knows" (Mark 13:32). A few days before his death, he is at dinner in Bethany when a woman breaks open a jar of very costly perfume and pours it over his head. Some guests are indignant. They say it could have been sold for the poor (Mark 14:5).

Jesus defends her: "Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me." Then he says what her gift means: "She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying." Whether or not she knew it, her love prepared him for his death. Jesus promises she will be remembered wherever the Good News is told.

**Reflection:** What is one generous, even extravagant, act of love you could offer Jesus or someone else this week?

*Study aid: in a similar scene, John's Gospel names the woman Mary, the sister of Martha and Lazarus (John 12:3). Many readers take the two accounts as the same event; Mark leaves her unnamed.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you are worth more than anything I could give. Help me love you generously and do what I can.

quiz.prompt: What did the woman pour over Jesus' head?
quiz.explain: Mark 14:3: "a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly."

quiz.prompt: How did Jesus respond to those who criticized her?
choices: You are right to be angry
quiz.explain: Mark 14:6: "Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me."

quiz.prompt: "She has done what she ___."
quiz.explain: Mark 14:8. Jesus honors what she was able to give.

lessons.title: This is my body
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
On the night before he dies, Jesus shares what Mark presents as the Passover meal with his disciples (Mark 14:12). He takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them: "Take, eat. This is my body." Then the cup: "This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many."

Jesus uses an ordinary meal to speak about his death. With the bread and the cup, he speaks of his body and his blood, given for many. The meal also looks ahead: he will drink it "anew in God’s Kingdom" (Mark 14:25). Christians have kept doing what Jesus did at this table ever since.

**Reflection:** Jesus says his blood is poured out for many. Take a moment to thank him that this includes you.

*Study aid: Christians call this meal Communion, the Lord's Supper or the Eucharist, and understand it in different ways. All trace it back to this night.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, thank you for giving yourself for many, and for me. Help me remember you.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus say as he gave them the bread?
choices: This is the bread of Passover
Remember the manna in the desert
Take, eat. This is my body
quiz.explain: Mark 14:22: "Take, eat. This is my body."

quiz.prompt: "This is my blood of the new ___, which is poured out for many."
quiz.explain: Mark 14:24. Jesus speaks of a new covenant.

quiz.prompt: For whom does Jesus say his blood is poured out?
quiz.explain: Mark 14:24: "which is poured out for many."

lessons.title: Not what I desire
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
In Gethsemane, Jesus begins to be "greatly troubled and distressed." He tells his closest friends, "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death." Mark does not hide Jesus' anguish.

Then he prays: "Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire." He asks honestly for another way, and he trusts his Father with the answer. Both are in the same prayer. Meanwhile, the disciples keep falling asleep (Mark 14:37). Jesus wakes them and tells them to watch and pray: "The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."

**Reflection:** Is there something you are asking God to take away? Can you pray both halves of Jesus' prayer about it today?

*Study aid: "Abba" is the Aramaic word for father, used within families. Paul says Christians pray with the same word (Romans 8:15).*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Abba, Father, you know what I am asking. Not what I desire, but what you desire. Give me strength.

quiz.prompt: How did Jesus describe his soul in Mark 14:34?
quiz.explain: Mark 14:34: "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death."

quiz.prompt: "However, not what I desire, but what you ___."
quiz.explain: Mark 14:36. Jesus asks honestly and trusts his Father.

quiz.prompt: What did Jesus say about his sleeping disciples?
choices: Let them sleep; they cannot help
The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak
They do not care what happens
quiz.explain: Mark 14:38: "The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."

lessons.title: Before the rooster crows
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Earlier that night Peter was sure of himself: "Although all will be offended, yet I will not." Jesus told him that before the rooster crowed twice, he would deny him three times.

Now Peter is in the high priest's courtyard, warming himself by the fire (Mark 14:66). A servant girl recognizes him. Three times he denies knowing Jesus, the last time with curses: "I don’t know this man of whom you speak!" Then the rooster crows a second time. Peter remembers Jesus' words, and he weeps. Mark tells this failure plainly, without softening it.

**Reflection:** Have you ever failed someone you love, or failed God, in a way that still hurts? Hold on to that as you read the last two lessons. Peter's story does not end here.

*Study aid: an early Christian writer, Papias, said that Mark wrote down Peter's memories of Jesus. Scholars weigh this tradition in different ways.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you know my failures and you still call me. Thank you that my story doesn't end with them.

quiz.prompt: What did Peter say when Jesus warned that the disciples would stumble?
choices: Lord, I am afraid I will
Although all will be offended, yet I will not
Tell us when it will happen
Then we must all run away
quiz.explain: Mark 14:29. Peter was sure of his own strength.

quiz.prompt: How many times did Jesus say Peter would deny him?
quiz.explain: Mark 14:30: "before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times."

quiz.prompt: What did Peter do when he remembered Jesus' words?
quiz.explain: Mark 14:72: "When he thought about that, he wept."

lessons.title: Truly the Son of God
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
After a night of questioning, Pilate hands Jesus over to be crucified (Mark 15:15). At midday, darkness covers the land for three hours. Then Jesus cries out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" These are the opening words of Psalm 22, a psalm that begins in abandonment and ends in praise. Even on the cross, Jesus prays the Psalms.

Jesus cries out again and dies. Then someone speaks, and in Mark it is not one of his disciples but the Roman centurion who watched him die: "Truly this man was the Son of God!" Mark's first line called Jesus "the Son of God" (Mark 1:1). Here, at the cross, an outsider says it.

**Reflection:** Take a quiet minute with this scene. What do you want to say to Jesus?

*Study aid: Mark notes that women who had followed Jesus from Galilee were watching from a distance (Mark 15:40). They will be the first at the tomb.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Jesus, you went into the darkness for us. Thank you. Truly you are the Son of God.

quiz.prompt: What happened from the sixth hour until the ninth hour?
choices: a bright light in the sky
quiz.explain: Mark 15:33: "there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour."

quiz.prompt: "My God, my God, why have you ___ me?"
quiz.explain: Mark 15:34. Jesus cries out the first words of Psalm 22.

quiz.prompt: What did the centurion say when he saw how Jesus died?
choices: Truly this man was the Son of God!
This man was a prophet of Galilee
This man was only a teacher
Surely this man was a criminal
quiz.explain: Mark 15:39: "Truly this man was the Son of God!"

lessons.title: He goes before you
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Very early on the first day of the week, three women come to the tomb with spices, wondering who will roll away the heavy stone (Mark 16:3). It has already been rolled back. A young man in white tells them, "He has risen! He is not here."

Then he gives them a message: "go, tell his disciples and Peter." Peter, who denied Jesus three times, is named. Jesus is going ahead of them into Galilee, where the story began. The women flee, trembling and amazed. Mark leaves the story open, as if handing it to the reader: will you go and meet him too?

You have walked through Mark from "The beginning of the Good News" (Mark 1:1) to an empty tomb. Consider reading it again in the Bible tab. It reads differently the second time.

**Reflection:** Peter was named, after everything. What does it mean to you that Jesus' invitation includes people who have failed him?

*Study aid: the oldest manuscripts of Mark end at 16:8. Most Bibles, including the WEB text in this app, also include verses 9 to 20, often with a note.*
lessons.prayerPrompt: Risen Jesus, thank you that you go ahead of me, and that your invitation includes me. Help me follow you.

quiz.prompt: What did the young man in the tomb tell the women?
choices: He has gone up to the temple
He has risen! He is not here
quiz.explain: Mark 16:6: "He has risen! He is not here. See the place where they laid him!"

quiz.prompt: Whom did the young man name, along with the disciples?
quiz.explain: Mark 16:7: "But go, tell his disciples and Peter."

quiz.prompt: Where did the young man say Jesus was going ahead of them?
quiz.explain: Mark 16:7: "He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you."
